question: What are the best alternatives to LinkedIn Learning for enterprise upskilling?
text:
If your goal is enterprise-wide upskilling, rather than simply replacing LinkedIn Learning’s course library, I’d shortlist these:

Platform	Best for	Biggest advantage	Watch-out
Coursera for Business	Broad workforce transformation	University/company credentials + structured skill paths	Less “just-in-time” breadth than Udemy
Udemy Business	Broad, practical upskilling	Huge catalog and fast coverage of emerging skills	Course quality can be more variable
Pluralsight	Engineering, cloud, AI, cybersecurity	Deep technical skills assessment + hands-on labs	Narrower outside technical roles
O’Reilly for Business	Technical/professional teams	Exceptional depth, books, live experts, labs	Not as strong for general corporate skills
Skillsoft Percipio	Large L&D organizations	Skills intelligence + learning + talent development	Can be more complex to implement
360Learning	Internal knowledge + collaborative learning	Employees/SMEs can create and share organizational knowledge	More of an LMS/LXP than a pure content marketplace
My ranking

1. Coursera for Business — best overall alternative

This would be my first evaluation if you're replacing LinkedIn Learning for a large, diverse workforce. Coursera combines courses from universities and companies, Professional Certificates, role-based Skills Tracks, skills benchmarking and enterprise analytics. Its current business catalog includes 10,600+ courses, 1,400+ specializations and 165+ Professional Certificates. 
C
Coursera
+1

Best for: digital transformation, AI/data, business skills, leadership, professional credentials, global organizations.

Coursera for Business

2. Udemy Business — best for breadth and practical skills

Udemy is particularly attractive if employees need to learn whatever technology or business skill is relevant right now. Its Enterprise offering has 30,000+ curated courses, assessments, learning paths, analytics, proprietary-content capabilities and content in 16 languages. 
U
Udemy Business
+1

The major advantage over LinkedIn Learning is the sheer variety and speed with which niche/emerging topics appear.

Best for: large heterogeneous workforces, developers, business users, AI adoption, emerging technologies.

Udemy Business

3. Pluralsight — best for technical upskilling

If a significant part of your workforce is engineers, developers, cloud specialists or security professionals, I'd put Pluralsight ahead of both LinkedIn Learning and Udemy. It combines skills/role assessments with structured paths, 3,500+ hands-on labs, cloud/AI sandboxes, certification preparation and enterprise analytics. 
P
Pluralsight

Best for: software engineering, cloud, cybersecurity, DevOps, data and AI.

Pluralsight for Enterprise

4. O’Reilly — best for serious technical organizations

O'Reilly is particularly compelling for engineering-heavy companies. Its enterprise platform currently offers 75,000+ resources, nearly 200 live expert events per month, labs/sandboxes, AI-powered answers and role/skill-based learning. 
O
O'Reilly Media
+1

It's less of a generic corporate-learning supermarket and more of a deep technical knowledge platform.

Best for: engineering, architecture, AI, data, cloud, security and technically sophisticated teams.

O’Reilly for Business

5. Skillsoft Percipio — best for mature L&D/skills programs

Skillsoft is worth considering if you're trying to move beyond "employees watched X hours of training" toward a skills-based workforce strategy. Percipio connects learning content, skills data, proficiency measurement and workforce insights in one platform, with AI-driven recommendations and skills inference. 
S
Skillsoft Corporation

Best for: large enterprises with sophisticated L&D, skills management, leadership and compliance requirements.

6. 360Learning — best for internal knowledge sharing

This is the wildcard. Rather than relying primarily on an external course library, 360Learning focuses heavily on turning your own employees' expertise into learning. Its platform combines LMS/LXP functionality, AI-assisted content creation, collaborative authoring, skills recommendations and enterprise analytics.

Best for: organizations where internal processes, products and proprietary knowledge are as important as generic skills.

Need one platform for the whole company: Coursera

Want maximum breadth and practical "learn what I need today": Udemy Business

Upskilling engineers/IT: Pluralsight

Best technical knowledge resource: O'Reilly

Building a sophisticated skills-based L&D function: Skillsoft Percipio

Capturing and scaling internal expertise: 360Learning

One important distinction: LinkedIn Learning is primarily a content destination; some of these alternatives are much more ambitious workforce-skills platforms. If your objective is strategic enterprise upskilling—skills inventory → identify gaps → assign learning → assess proficiency → demonstrate business impact—I'd evaluate Coursera, Pluralsight, Skillsoft and 360Learning rather than comparing course counts alone.

If you tell me your company size, main employee groups (e.g. engineering vs. sales vs. leadership), and whether AI upskilling is a priority, I can narrow this to a top 3 with an enterprise procurement-style comparison of pricing, content, integrations, analytics, AI capabilities and ROI.
